chapter: Brass band style, leadership and recording
title: The Olympia t-shirt, Roman collar uniforms and insisting on dress
summary: The first brass band t-shirt from a Toronto trip and the uniforms still used, plus his insistence on dressing well.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: You know what I'm saying? I went back to the old fireman's cap, which was used in the early days for the circus band and the other bands that performed. And to me, musicians should be dressed. All the time be dressed. And I stress this with my band up to today. Don't come on my bandstand and don't come with me on a parade. If you're not dressed the way I ask you to dress. Paul Crawford's wife invented and made the first brass band t-shirt in New Orleans. She copied it from a t-shirt that was given to us in the early 60s from Toronto, Canada. We went to Toronto, Canada, Arrow, Dajon, and Olympia Brass Band. And they made a t-shirt for us to wear because it was so nice and warm. And it read, Dajon's Olympia Brass Band. It had a steamboat in the middle. It had three colors, red, green, and black on a white shirt. That shirt and Joji Mellie made our first brass band uniforms. And we paid half price. He donated the other half. Suits cost us like $200. We only had to pay him $100. It was a Roman collar. Made like a, something like a priest's collar. And those uniforms, as you can see in that picture up there, we still use those today. Those things have brought us many jobs. It brought us notoriety and everything else as being the only band out of Sydney, New Orleans, who dresses like that, authentically. Today, you got brass bands. And I'm not ashamed to say that one of my protégés, like the young Olympians, who are the soul rebels, they come on the street or they come on a gig dressed like nothing. Damn it to hell, that's what they look like.

And it's not representative of a musician. Even in my younger days, whenever I saw musicians perform at 2Kalindicom, Basie, Luckett, Melinda, any bands, they were dressed. Sharp looking. They were serious. Yeah. Oh, yeah, you look the best. You know?
Even when you were on the road, you know, for sure, that must have been very difficult for you all to always have clean, pressed clothes.

We did it. Even in rhythm and blues bands and so forth. We always managed to have a red coat alike, an orange coat, a brown suit, a shirt, something alike. And I will always emphatically impress on my musicians that they must come looking presentable. That's part of it.
